result.summary:
Verdict PASS. Narrow pass 3 over git diff bddef13 5c85759: the one code change is app/server/db/pg.js (+20 lines); the rest is decisions/0137 Addition 5, design section 7 and 19 rows, and handoffs. No finding of any severity that blocks; no Low finding either.
Listener present exactly while the client is held: it is attached right after pool.connect() succeeds (a failed connect has no client and throws as before) and removed on the normal release by client.off after client.release(false), so the pool's own idle listener takes over. On a drop (the error path, or the flag set before a normal release) the client is released with release(true) and keeps the listener while it ends, so a late event of its socket cannot end the process either. There is exactly one release per path (the error path releases in finally after the not-awaited rollback settles; the normal path releases once), so no double-release.
Dropped client released as broken: the error handler only sets a flag; run() then throws DbError E_DB_DOWN before sending any statement, and a statement in flight is rejected by pg itself and mapped by toDbError; the throw goes through the unchanged rollback-then-release(true) path. A drop that happens after the last statement but before release makes release(false) become release(true) (gone = drop || broken).
No error swallowed beyond the 503 path, nothing logged: onError is a one-line flag setter that discards the error object, so neither its message nor the connection text can reach a log (the pipeline's log line holds the code only); there is no console call. The idle-client swallow pool.on('error', () => {}) is the earlier one and is unchanged.
Normal, rollback and plain-query paths unchanged: the diff leaves query(), exec(), the begin/commit/rollback sequence, COMMIT_LIMIT_MS, the throw of fn passing unchanged and close() untouched; the only edits inside transaction() are the listener, the broken check in run() and the two release calls.
Own probe on a checkout of 5c85759 (a stub Postgres speaking the simple protocol on port 0 under <scratch>, stopped in the same script; no real database, no repository test). Old pg.js (bddef13) against the same stub: uncaught 'Connection terminated unexpectedly', process exit 3 (the defect reproduced). New pg.js: drop while the transaction waits between statements -> DbError E_DB_DOWN in 178 ms; drop in the middle of a statement -> E_DB_DOWN in 4 ms; no uncaught exception; the process lives; a normal transaction returns its value; 30 more normal transactions on the same pool give no MaxListenersExceededWarning (the listener does not pile up on pooled clients).
Own checks: prettier --check . exit 0; eslint . --max-warnings 0 exit 0; tsc --noEmit -p jsconfig.json exit 0; import-boundaries findings for server [] and fileFindings []; stringSql [] (DbError imported from ./index.js, the same file that already exports toDbError). Erosion grep over pg.js: no match; no CR. cd tools && npm run -s traces: 0 traces; handoffs-check: 0 violations.
For TEST-DESIGNER: ADD-4 as named in section 19 (a cut connection answers 503 db_unavailable within 5 s, no uncaught error, the app keeps serving) is enough; my stub can only be run on the pg job path for the real pool, but the behaviour is reproducible without Postgres as shown.
